inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to deploy or migrate in production on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions under engineer identity
Chat transcript history exists but engineers can delete it
controls.decay_rationale: This record does not provide durable attribution because the acting engineer can delete it, so it does not restore repudiation.

controls.name: Missing tamper-resistant agent action provenance bound to human request and agent execution

findings.title: Missing attributable provenance for production actions recorded only under the engineer's identity

evidence.observation: Production actions are recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name rather than under a distinct agent identity or dual attribution.
The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.
The prompt authorizes deploy and migration actions on request and says not to ask for confirmation, so the design depends on attributable records after action rather than approval before action.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making one affected capability S3 and causing the property finding to score from the I row at high under rubric section 5a.

recommendations.action: Add tamper-resistant action provenance that binds the authenticated engineer request, exact tool arguments, agent identity, timestamps, and resulting production action into an append-only record that engineers cannot delete or rewrite.
Record production actions under both a distinct agent/service identity and the requesting engineer identity so investigators can distinguish direct human action from agent-mediated action.
Retain immutable copies of request transcripts or signed action receipts outside user-deletable chat history for incident investigation.

forecast.watch_signal: Raise the agent's autonomy, broaden its production duties, or remove existing logs/transcript retention assumptions; reassess if production actions become more autonomous or less attributable.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no self-modification path, tool-definition updates, or writable configuration surface for this agent design.
The design includes no read or egress capability for sensitive data beyond production actions, so no disclosure path is evidenced in the supplied artifacts.
No looping, spending, delegation, or unbounded runtime behavior is described, so a service exhaustion property finding is not evidenced here.
The agent uses the requesting engineer's delegated credentials rather than broader shared or elevated credentials in the described design.
The artifacts do not describe transport integrity, command signing, or deployment API request integrity for the production deploy flow.
This boundary-crossing flow performs a deployment action and the supplied artifacts do not show it carrying sensitive data to an external recipient.
No step limits, retry loops, or high-volume autonomous deployment behavior are described for this flow in the provided design notes.
The artifacts do not describe transport integrity, command signing, or migration API request integrity for the production migration flow.
This boundary-crossing flow executes a migration and the supplied artifacts do not evidence disclosure of sensitive data to an outside recipient.
The materials describe irreversible migrations but do not describe runaway execution volume or resource exhaustion on this flow.
The artifacts do not state transcript access controls, retention scope, or whether one engineer can access another engineer's history.
The design issue with this store is deletability and attribution loss, not store exhaustion or availability loss, in the supplied evidence.
The artifacts say actions are recorded in the cloud audit log but do not describe immutability, retention locks, or write protection for the log.
The artifacts do not describe who can read audit records or whether log payloads include sensitive deployment or migration arguments.
No evidence suggests quota exhaustion or logging outages are a salient risk in this narrow design review.

rating.rationale: Single present property finding: the design lacks attributable, tamper-resistant provenance separating agent-mediated production actions from direct engineer actions. Existing records are detective only and do not restore repudiation because the cloud audit log attributes actions solely to the engineer and the only request context is user-deletable chat history. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, IaC, or detailed runtime configuration was provided, so transport integrity, transcript retention implementation, and cloud audit log immutability could not be verified.
No tool manifest or API schema was provided, so capability details were inferred from the narrative artifacts.
